```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("rmorie", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

A capsule is a directory holding a data file and `data_provenance.json`, the record of where
the file came from and what it was: its SHA-256, size and row count. The record is what lets
someone else (or you, a year later) confirm that an analysis still runs on the data it was
written for. The `morie_capsule_*()` functions are thin wrappers over rmoriebricklayer; the same
capsules are read by morie in Python and checked in CI by the `rmbl-action` GitHub Action.

```{r}
library(rmorie)
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "capsule-vignette")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(1)
utils::write.csv(data.frame(region = sample(c("east", "west"), 200, TRUE),
                            rate = stats::rnorm(200, 10, 2)),
                 file.path(dir, "rates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Write the record

```{r}
prov <- morie_capsule_write(dir, "rates.csv", url = "https://example.org/rates.csv",
                            name = "rates", retrieved = "2026-10-20")
str(prov$resource)
```

## Verify it

Every check is a row; `ok` is `TRUE` only when all of them pass.

```{r}
morie_capsule_verify(dir)
```

## Record the results, sign and bundle

The manifest records the numbers the analysis produced next to the numbers they should
reproduce. Signing it, or bundling the whole directory, shows who vouched for the capsule and
that nothing changed since.

```{r}
d <- utils::read.csv(file.path(dir, "rates.csv"))
man <- suppressMessages(morie_capsule_manifest(
  list(project = "rates"),
  data.frame(name = c("n", "mean_rate"), observed = c(nrow(d), mean(d$rate)),
             expected = c(200, mean(d$rate))),
  path = file.path(dir, "manifest.json")
))
key <- rmoriebricklayer::fipskg("ML-DSA-44")
sig <- morie_capsule_sign(man, key)
rmoriebricklayer::cpsvrf(rmoriebricklayer::mnfdgst(man), sig, key)
bundle <- morie_capsule_bundle(dir, man, key)
rmoriebricklayer::cpsbndlvrf(attr(bundle, "path"), dir, man = man)$ok
morie_capsule_compare(man, d, list(n = nrow, mean_rate = function(z) mean(z$rate)))$ok
```

## Check a fresh download for drift

A re-released file has a new digest even when it holds the same data; `morie_capsule_drift()`
asks whether the distributions moved.

```{r}
fresh <- d
fresh$rate <- fresh$rate * 1.5
drift <- morie_capsule_drift(dir, fresh)
drift$anydrft
drift$columns[, c("column", "type", "p_value", "drifted")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
